transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 56 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Fernandez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO - Octant), Samir Patel (ML Eng), Evan Brooks (Infra), Lina Park (Security)

Summary: initial discovery to decide between Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private for Octant's conversational product. Focus: model selection (open models), context length (32k vs 100k), multilingual support (EN, JP, FR), tool-calling (DB lookup, run-book retrieval), and security/compliance constraints (VPC, KMS, audit logs).

Topics:
- Current infra and pain points
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs for 1K-40K token asks
- Private deployment requirements and timeline
- Tool-calling patterns and reliability needs

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — i'm maya, i look after accounts in the fintech / infra space at Redwood. diego's our solutions engineer and he'll walk through the technical stuff. do you want to do quick intros?
[00:12] Priya (CTO): sure, priya here. CTO at Octant. we build a conversational ops assistant for enterprise networks, so we have high context needs and some regulatory constraints.
[00:20] Samir (ML Eng): samir — i own models and evals, mostly fine-tuning and prompt templates.
[00:24] Evan (Infra): evan, infra lead, networking/VPCs, deployment pipelines.
[00:28] Lina (Security): lina, security/compliance, i'll be driving SOC2 questions and KMS integration.
[00:32] Diego (SE): great, thanks. quick agenda: three parts — existing stack and constraints, model+context needs, and then tool-calling plus next steps.

[02:10] Priya: to start, our main question is whether we go hosted for faster time to market, or reserved/dedicated (predictable latency), or private on-prem for data residency. we have about 8M monthly queries with a tail of long-context sessions — maybe 5-8% of requests hit 20k-40k tokens. some sessions could reach 75-100k during incident reconstructions.
[02:35] Maya: ok that helps. when you say 75-100k, is that full model context or you chunk and stream?
[02:41] Priya: currently we chunk, but it hurts coherence. we want a model that can reasonably ingest 50-100k prefixes without manual chunking if possible.

[04:00] Diego: technically, very few open weights handle >64k efficiently without specialized kernel support. we have two paths: use a model variant with extended context (Redwood supports several curated open models and some quantized variants) or use prefix/KV caching + retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that keeps active session KV cache and pulls older history from a vector DB.
[04:25] Samir: what about 100k context on dedicated infra — does Redwood have a tested path?
[04:30] Diego: we've run internal experiments on 100k using concat+kv eviction and sparse attention kernels on specific backends. results are mixed — latency jumps and memory usage is high. for a production SLA we'd recommend a hybrid: increase model context to 32k-65k where feasible and rely on RAG + smart summarization for older history.
[05:02] Priya: so 32k sounds like a practical target. keys: low latency for interactive sessions (<350ms 95th) for short queries, and tolerable higher latency for long-history reconstruction.

[06:10] Evan: on infra, we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. also audit logs retained for 7 years (regulatory). can Redwood's private option support air-gapped on-prem installs?
[06:25] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports an on-prem package and VPC deployments. the private plane can be configured behind your KMS/HSM. i'll share the on-prem checklist after call, with network ports, k8s requirements et cetera.
[06:45] Lina: about audit logs — we need immutable logs and SSO (SAML) integration. also RBAC across teams.
[06:52] Diego: Redwood Console supports token-level cost and request tracing; audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM. SSO via SAML/SCIM is supported. small caveat: some on-prem installations require additional config for long-term retention — we usually push logs to customer-managed object storage.

[08:10] Samir: model selection: we're leaning open-source models. we evaluated Llama-family forks and a couple of 30B/70B variants. what's Redwood's stance on open model catalog and quantization?
[08:25] Diego: Redwood maintains a curated catalog with performance profiles. we recommend models that have strong long-context engineering; for 32k use-cases a 70B quantized variant often balances quality and cost. for multilingual support (EN/JP/FR), check model tokenizers — some models degrade on japanese. we can run a multilingual eval with your prompts.
[08:52] Priya: our budget is middle-of-the-road — we can't afford OpenAI's larger rates at scale. price sensitivity pushes us toward dedicated or private with reserved capacity to control per-token cost.
[09:10] Maya: yep, that's common — dedicated_reserved gives predictable throughput and unit economics, private can reduce egress and be cheaper at very large scale but has upfront ops cost. hosted is fastest to prototype.

[11:00] Evan: latency targets — sub-350ms for short (<=512 tokens) paths and 1-2s acceptable for 8-32k streaming. do you do continuous batching that preserves latency SLOs?
[11:14] Diego: our serving runtime uses continuous batching with policy knobs — you can set max latency target and batch aggressiveness. for high-priority routes we route to low-latency pools. there are trade-offs with cost.

[12:50] Priya: tool-calling is huge — we need reliable DB lookups, run-book invocation, and the ability to call internal tools with structured output. can Redwood do function/tool calling and ensure deterministic fallback when external tools time out?
[13:05] Diego: yes — streaming function calling is supported, and you can define timeouts and fallbacks. we also support structured output schemas. for offline replays we capture tool call traces in the console. note: transcription sometimes says function calling as tool calling — but yes, same feature.
[14:00] Samir: what's the guarantee if a tool call fails mid-generation — do you have automatic retry or graceful degrade to cached content?
[14:08] Diego: there are policy-driven fallbacks: retry, use cached result, or return a non-blocking response. you can configure per-route policies.

[16:20] Lina: security question — we require BYOK (bring-your-own-key) and HSM-backed key rotation. KMS must be customer-controlled. can we do that in Hosted?
[16:34] Maya: hosted supports customer-managed keys for encryption at rest via KMS integrations in certain plans; for full control and isolation, Private is recommended. we'll attach the SOC2 doc and KMS integration notes.
[17:02] Priya: also data residency — some EU customers require data to stay in eu. can we pin region?
[17:08] Diego: yes, you can pin region routing policies. Redwood routes by policy and supports geo-isolation for customers.

[19:00] Priya: question on multilingual — our top issues: tokenizer mismatch with Japanese, and hallucination on translated prompts. do you recommend separate fine-tuned models per language or single multilingual model?
[19:16] Samir: yeah we debate that — separate models are heavier but can be optimized for tokenization and reduce hallucination. multilingual models can be ok if trained/fine-tuned on your corpora.
[19:40] Diego: pragmatic approach: run a language-wise eval. for JP, often a 13B+ with proper tokenizer beat generic 70B out-of-the-box. we can run benchmark with your prompt set, measure quality metrics (bleu/rouge-ish and hallucination evals).

[22:10] Priya: okay can you run a 32k context test with our incident logs and a multilingual sample?
[22:16] Diego: yes, please send sample prompts and a sanitized log set. we will spin up a dedicated pool for the benchmark. note the perf numbers vary by quantization and hw.

[24:00] Evan: on telemetry — we need per-route token billing and per-user tracing. is that out-of-the-box?
[24:09] Maya: console gives token-level cost breakdowns and tracers; you can export traces to an external system.

[26:30] Priya: timeline — we'd like to decide in 3 weeks and pilot in early q1. must pass security review.
[26:38] Lina: we have a security questionnaire (30+ pages) and need an on-site audit possibility.
[26:44] Maya: understood. we'll send SOC2, penetration test summaries, and an on-prem checklist. we can also schedule a security deep-dive with our compliance lead.

[29:00] Samir: pricing asks — what's ballpark per-token for hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[29:08] Maya: hosted is highest per-token but lowest operational overhead; dedicated reserved pools give discounts for commits; private is more capex but lowest marginal cost at scale. i'll send a cost model spreadsheet after call with scenarios (we'll include an example 8M monthly usage calculation).

[31:10] Diego: technical caveat — for 32k context we often recommend a memory-optimized GPU (A100 or similar) or multi-GPU sharding. private deployments may require different node sizing. we'll include a recommended config.

[33:45] Priya: there was mention of KV cache earlier — is that maintained per session and does it survive restarts?
[33:55] Diego: KV cache is per-session and stored in the serving layer; for restarts you'd rely on warmup or persistent cache backed by a fast store. we can add warmstart procedures for dedicated pools. some transcripts accidentally say KVC ash, so apologies to the transcript.

[36:05] Evan: operationally, how do you handle model rollouts — can we canary across a subset of traffic?
[36:12] Diego: yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies to previous model versions on regression.

[38:00] Priya: any gotchas with function calling and private deployments — latency between model and tool endpoints inside VPC?
[38:10] Diego: you control network topology in private. we recommend colocating tool endpoints in same VPC/subnet. hosted requires secure tunnels to your private tools; that adds latency and you'll want to benchmark.

[41:40] Priya: ok let's put it together — we want: 1) Redwood to run 32k context benchmark with our data 2) security packet and SOC2 3) cost model for 8M monthly queries and reserved capacity vs private.
[41:55] Maya: yep — action items noted. diego will run perf tests; i'll send security + pricing docs.

[44:20] Samir: one more — do you support model quantization and half-precision variants that change latency profiles?
[44:28] Diego: yes we support quantized variants and can test int8/int4 profiles. quality impact varies; we'll include quality tradeoffs in the benchmark report.

[47:50] Lina: compliance: what about e-discovery for logs — can we extract user-level data for audits?
[47:58] Diego: audit exports can be configured, but in hosted you may need additional access. in private you control retention policies more directly.

[50:00] Priya: sounds good. can we get rough SLA numbers for Dedicated (p95/p99 latency)?
[50:05] Maya: typical p95 for dedicated pools on short tokens is ~200-300ms, p99 depends on model and load. we'll include target SLAs per config.

[52:30] Evan: ok final — send links to docs?
[52:35] Maya: i'll send: SOC2 + penetration test summary (link), on-prem checklist (link), and a shared benchmark spreadsheet. links: https://redwood.example/security-packet , https://redwood.example/onprem-checklist , https://redwood.example/pricing-scenarios

[54:20] Priya: thanks all. we'll put together the prompt set and traffic profile. anticipate next call in ~1 week for perf results.
[54:30] Maya: great, thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
